source_refs.note: Exercise 3.2 Q2 (i)-(xiii), by change of variable; answers printed in the key block 'Exercise 3.4'

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein \(e^{2x}\) dekh kar ghabrana nahi: \(e^{2x} = (e^{x})^{2}\).
Upar \(e^{x}dx\) pada hai, jo \(e^{x}\) ka differential hai.
To \(u = e^{x}\) rakhte hi integral \(\int\frac{du}{9-u^{2}}\) ban jata hai, yani \(\frac{1}{a^{2}-u^{2}}\) wala special integral, \(a = 3\).
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: change of variable, formula, phir \(x\) wapas.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = e^{x}\) rakhenge, phir Section 3.3 ka special integral \(\int\frac{du}{a^{2}-u^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{a+u}{a-u}\right| + c\). Yeh formula is liye kaam aata hai ke denominator 'square minus square' ki shakal mein hai.

Change of variable
\[u = e^{x},\quad du = e^{x}\,dx\]
\[e^{2x} = (e^{x})^{2} = u^{2}\]
Kyun: \(e^{x}\) ka derivative \(e^{x}\) hi hai, is liye numerator \(e^{x}dx\) bilkul \(du\) ban gaya.

Special integral, \(a = 3\)
\[\int\dfrac{du}{3^{2}-u^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2(3)}\ln\left|\dfrac{3+u}{3-u}\right| + c\]
Kyun: \(9 = 3^{2}\), to denominator \(a^{2} - u^{2}\) hai jahan \(a = 3\).
Dhyan dein: \(a^{2} - u^{2}\) mein fraction \(\frac{a+u}{a-u}\) hota hai; \(u^{2} - a^{2}\) mein \(\frac{u-a}{u+a}\). In dono ko mila dena aam ghalti hai.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\ln\left|\dfrac{3+e^{x}}{3-e^{x}}\right| + c\]
Kyun: \(u = e^{x}\) wapas rakha.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{6}\big(\ln|3+e^{x}| - \ln|3-e^{x}|\big)\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\Big(\dfrac{e^{x}}{3+e^{x}} + \dfrac{e^{x}}{3-e^{x}}\Big)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\cdot\dfrac{6e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}} = \dfrac{e^{x}}{9-e^{2x}}\]
Kyun: \(\ln\) ke quotient ko do \(\ln\) mein toda, derivative liya, aur asal integrand mil gaya.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Answer key is sawal ke jawab 'Exercise 3.4' ki heading ke neeche chhapti hai ('Exercise 3.2' wali heading ke neeche asal mein Exercise 3.5 ke jawab hain).
Q2 (i)-(viii) wahan 1 (i)-(viii) hain; Q2 (x), (xi), (xii) apne hi number par hain; Q2 (ix) wahan (xiv) aur Q2 (xiii) wahan (xv) chhapa hai.
Key ke (ix) \(2 - \frac{\pi}{2}\) aur (xiii) \(\frac{\pi}{8}\ln 2\) definite integrals ki values hain jo is exercise ke kisi sawal ki nahi.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x-4}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Upar \(\cos x\) aur neeche \(\sin^{2}x\): yeh jori foran batati hai ke \(u = \sin x\) lo, kyunke \(\cos x\,dx = d(\sin x)\).
Phir integral \(\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-4}\) ban jata hai.
Yeh 'variable ka square minus constant ka square' hai, yani Challenge box ka formula (i), \(a = 2\).
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: change of variable, formula, \(x\) wapas.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x-4}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = \sin x\), phir formula \(\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-a^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{u-a}{u+a}\right| + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = \sin x,\quad du = \cos x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(\sin x\) ka derivative \(\cos x\); numerator poora \(du\) ban gaya.

Formula lagayein, \(a = 2\)
\[\int\dfrac{du}{u^{2}-2^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2(2)}\ln\left|\dfrac{u-2}{u+2}\right| + c\]
Kyun: \(4 = 2^{2}\), denominator \(u^{2} - a^{2}\) ki shakal mein hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan pehle \(u^{2}\) hai phir \(a^{2}\), is liye fraction \(\frac{u-a}{u+a}\) hai; part (i) mein tarteeb ulti thi.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\ln\left|\dfrac{\sin x-2}{\sin x+2}\right| + c\]
Kyun: \(u = \sin x\). Kyunke \(\sin x\) hamesha \(-1\) aur 1 ke darmiyan hai, \(\sin x - 2\) negative aur \(\sin x + 2\) positive rehta hai; is liye yeh \(\frac{1}{4}\ln\frac{2-\sin x}{2+\sin x} + c\) bhi likha ja sakta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{4}\big(\ln|\sin x-2| - \ln|\sin x+2|\big)\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos x}{4}\Big(\dfrac{1}{\sin x-2} - \dfrac{1}{\sin x+2}\Big)\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos x}{4}\cdot\dfrac{4}{\sin^{2}x-4} = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x-4}\]
Kyun: asal integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh part (i) jaisa hi hai, bas denominator mein minus ki jagah plus hai.
\(u = e^{x}\) rakhne se \(\int\frac{du}{1+u^{2}}\) banta hai.
'Ek square plus doosra square' ka matlab hai \(\tan^{-1}\) wala formula.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: substitution, phir \(\tan^{-1}\) formula, \(a = 1\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}\,dx\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = e^{x}\), phir \(\int\frac{du}{a^{2}+u^{2}} = \frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{u}{a} + c\), \(a = 1\).

Change of variable
\[u = e^{x},\quad du = e^{x}\,dx\]
\[\int\dfrac{e^{x}\,dx}{1+(e^{x})^{2}} = \int\dfrac{du}{1+u^{2}}\]
Kyun: numerator \(du\) ban gaya aur \(e^{2x} = u^{2}\).

Integrate karein aur \(x\) wapas likhein
\[= \tan^{-1}u + c = \tan^{-1}(e^{x}) + c\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1}u\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\) hai, to ulta chal kar yeh integral mila.
Dhyan dein: plus wale denominator mein \(\ln\) nahi aata; \(\ln\) wala formula sirf minus (square minus square) ke liye hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}(e^{x}) = \dfrac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}\]
Kyun: chain rule se integrand wapas mila. (Answer key \(\arctan(e^{x})\) likhti hai; \(\arctan\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) ek hi cheez hain.)

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{x\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(\frac{1}{x}\) aur \(\ln x\) saath hain; yeh jori hamesha \(u = \ln x\) ka ishara hai, kyunke \(d(\ln x) = \frac{dx}{x}\).
Phir integral \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{4-u^{2}}}\) banta hai.
Root ke andar 'constant square minus variable square' hai, yani \(\sin^{-1}\) wala special integral.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: substitution, \(\sin^{-1}\) formula \(a = 2\), \(x\) wapas.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = \ln x\), phir \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{a^{2}-u^{2}}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{u}{a} + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = \ln x,\quad du = \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\]
\[\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{x} = \int\dfrac{du}{\sqrt{2^{2}-u^{2}}}\]
Kyun: \(\ln x\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{x}\); is liye \(\frac{dx}{x}\) poora \(du\) ban gaya.

Integrate karein aur \(x\) wapas likhein
\[= \sin^{-1}\dfrac{u}{2} + c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\ln x}{2}\right) + c\]
Kyun: special integral (ii), \(a = 2\) (kyunke \(4 = 2^{2}\)).
Dhyan dein: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{u}{a}\) mein \(a\) se divide hota hai, \(a^{2}\) se nahi; \(\frac{\ln x}{4}\) likhna ghalat hoga.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{\ln x}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-\frac{(\ln x)^{2}}{4}}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2x}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{4-(\ln x)^{2}}}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{1 - \frac{p}{4}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4-p}\), aur 2 cancel ho gaye. Integrand mil gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{9x^{2}-25}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Denominator \(9x^{2} - 25\) ko ghor se dekhein: yeh \((3x)^{2} - 5^{2}\) hai, do squares ka farq.
Lekin formula mein variable ka coefficient 1 hona chahiye, is liye \(u = 3x\) rakhte hain.
Phir \(dx = \frac{du}{3}\) aata hai aur integral \(\frac{1}{3}\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-25}\) ban jata hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: \(u = 3x\), \(u^{2} - a^{2}\) wala formula \(a = 5\), \(x\) wapas.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{9x^{2}-25}\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = 3x\), phir \(\int\frac{du}{u^{2}-a^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{u-a}{u+a}\right| + c\).

Change of variable
\[u = 3x,\quad du = 3\,dx,\quad dx = \dfrac{du}{3}\]
\[\int\dfrac{dx}{(3x)^{2}-5^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\int\dfrac{du}{u^{2}-5^{2}}\]
Kyun: \(9x^{2} = (3x)^{2}\) aur \(25 = 5^{2}\). \(dx\) ko bhi \(du\) mein badalna zaroori hai.

Formula lagayein, \(a = 5\)
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2(5)}\ln\left|\dfrac{u-5}{u+5}\right| + c\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{30}\ln\left|\dfrac{u-5}{u+5}\right| + c\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{3}\) bahar wala aur \(\frac{1}{10}\) formula wala, mil kar \(\frac{1}{30}\).
Dhyan dein: \(dx = \frac{du}{3}\) wala \(\frac{1}{3}\) bhool jayein to jawab \(\frac{1}{10}\ln\ldots\) aata hai jo ghalat hai.

Wapas \(x\) likhein
\[= \dfrac{1}{30}\ln\left|\dfrac{3x-5}{3x+5}\right| + c\]
Kyun: \(u = 3x\).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{1}{30}\Big(\dfrac{3}{3x-5} - \dfrac{3}{3x+5}\Big)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{30}\cdot\dfrac{30}{9x^{2}-25}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{9x^{2}-25}\]
Kyun: jawab ka derivative asal integrand hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{3x^{2}-12}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Root ke andar \(3x^{2} - 12\) hai; pehle 3 common nikalein: \(\sqrt{3}\sqrt{x^{2}-4}\).
Ab \(\sqrt{x^{2}-2^{2}}\) bacha, jo Case 3 ki shakal hai: 'variable square minus constant square'.
Case 3 mein \(x = a\sec\theta\) rakhte hain, kyunke \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\) root ko khatam kar deta hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral; hum \(x > 2\) lete hain taa ke root real ho.
Plan: 3 bahar, \(x = 2\sec\theta\), integral \(\int d\theta\) ban jayega, phir wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{3x^{2}-12}}\), \(x > 2\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: trigonometric substitution, Case 3 (\(\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\) ke liye \(x = a\sec\theta\)). Wajah: Pythagorean identity \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\) root ko ek saaf term bana deti hai.

Root se common factor bahar nikalein
\[\sqrt{3x^{2}-12} = \sqrt{3(x^{2}-4)} = \sqrt{3}\sqrt{x^{2}-4}\]
\[I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\int\dfrac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{ab} = \sqrt{a}\sqrt{b}\). Ab root bilkul Case 3 ki shakal mein hai, \(a = 2\).

\(x = 2\sec\theta\) rakhein, \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = 2\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{x^{2}-4} = \sqrt{4\sec^{2}\theta - 4}\]
\[= 2\sqrt{\tan^{2}\theta} = 2\tan\theta\]
Kyun: \(\sec\theta\) ka derivative \(\sec\theta\tan\theta\). Root ke andar 4 common, phir \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\). Is interval mein \(\tan\theta\) positive hai, is liye modulus ki zaroorat nahi.

Simple kar ke integrate karein
\[I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\int\dfrac{2\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta}{(2\sec\theta)(2\tan\theta)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\int\dfrac{1}{2}\,d\theta = \dfrac{\theta}{2\sqrt{3}} + c\]
Kyun: \(\sec\theta\) aur \(\tan\theta\) upar neeche cancel ho gaye, sirf \(\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\) bacha. Yahi trigonometric substitution ka kamaal hai.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[\sec\theta = \dfrac{x}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = \sec^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[I = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + c\]
Kyun: substitution \(x = 2\sec\theta\) se hi \(\theta\) nikala.

Answer key wali shakal
\[\tan\theta = \sqrt{\sec^{2}\theta-1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}{2}\]
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}{2}\]
Kyun: is liye key ka \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\arctan\left(\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}{2}\right) + c\) bhi \(x > 2\) ke liye bilkul yahi jawab hai.
Dhyan dein: ek hi angle ko \(\sec^{-1}\) ya \(\tan^{-1}\) se likh sakte hain; exam mein koi bhi sahi shakal manzoor hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\sec^{-1}\tfrac{x}{2}\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\cdot\dfrac{2}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}\,x\sqrt{x^{2}-4}} = \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{3x^{2}-12}}\]
Kyun: \(x > a\) ke liye \(\frac{d}{dx}\sec^{-1}\frac{x}{a} = \frac{a}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\). Integrand wapas mil gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Denominator \(x^{2} + a^{2}\) hai, yani 'square plus square'. Yeh Case 2 ka ishara hai: \(x = a\tan\theta\).
Kyunke \(\tan^{2}\theta + 1 = \sec^{2}\theta\), denominator ek hi term \(a^{2}\sec^{2}\theta\) ban jata hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral; \(a > 0\) maan kar chalte hain.
Plan: substitute, \(\tan^{2}\theta = \sec^{2}\theta - 1\), phir wapas \(x\).
Aakhir mein ek chhota tareeqa bhi dekhenge: pehle divide kar lena.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\,dx\), \(a > 0\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: Case 2, \(x = a\tan\theta\). Wajah: identity \(\tan^{2}\theta + 1 = \sec^{2}\theta\) se \(x^{2} + a^{2}\) ek term ban jata hai.

\(x = a\tan\theta\) rakhein, \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = a\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[x^{2}+a^{2} = a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta + a^{2} = a^{2}\sec^{2}\theta\]
Kyun: \(\tan\theta\) ka derivative \(\sec^{2}\theta\). \(a^{2}\) common nikal kar identity lagayi.

Simple karein
\[\int\dfrac{a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta}{a^{2}\sec^{2}\theta}\cdot a\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[= a\int\tan^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
Kyun: \(a^{2}\) cancel, \(\sec^{2}\theta\) cancel; sirf \(a\tan^{2}\theta\) bacha.

Integrate karein
\[= a\int(\sec^{2}\theta - 1)\,d\theta\]
\[= a(\tan\theta - \theta) + c\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{2}\theta\) ka seedha formula nahi, lekin \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1\) likh kar dono terms aasan ho jate hain.
Dhyan dein: \(\int\tan^{2}\theta\,d\theta = \frac{\tan^{3}\theta}{3}\) likhna bohat aam ghalti hai; power rule sirf variable par lagta hai, \(\tan\theta\) par nahi.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[a\tan\theta = x,\quad \theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\]
\[= x - a\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) + c\]
Kyun: substitution \(x = a\tan\theta\) se.

Chhota tareeqa
\[\dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}} = 1 - \dfrac{a^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\]
\[\int = x - a^{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a} + c\]
Kyun: numerator mein \(a^{2}\) jama aur minus kiya: \(\frac{(x^{2}+a^{2}) - a^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\). Phir \(\tan^{-1}\) formula. Jawab wahi aaya.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[x - a\tan^{-1}\tfrac{x}{a}\Big] = 1 - \dfrac{a^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\]
Kyun: integrand wapas mil gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (viii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{x\left[1+(\ln x)^{2}\right]}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh part (iv) jaisa hai: \(\frac{1}{x}\) aur \(\ln x\) saath hain, to \(u = \ln x\).
Farq yeh hai ke yahan root nahi, aur denominator 'ek plus square' hai.
'Plus' wala denominator \(\tan^{-1}\) deta hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: substitution, \(\tan^{-1}\) formula, \(x\) wapas.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{x[1+(\ln x)^{2}]}\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(u = \ln x\), phir \(\tan^{-1}\) wala formula \(a = 1\).

Change of variable
\[u = \ln x,\quad du = \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
\[\int\dfrac{1}{1+(\ln x)^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{dx}{x} = \int\dfrac{du}{1+u^{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\ln x\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{x}\); \(\frac{dx}{x}\) poora \(du\) bana.

Integrate karein aur \(x\) wapas likhein
\[= \tan^{-1}u + c = \tan^{-1}(\ln x) + c\]
Kyun: \(\int\frac{du}{1+u^{2}} = \tan^{-1}u + c\).
Dhyan dein: \(\tan^{-1}(\ln x)\) ka matlab \(\ln x\) ka inverse tangent hai, \(\frac{1}{\tan(\ln x)}\) nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}(\ln x) = \dfrac{1}{1+(\ln x)^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\]
Kyun: chain rule se integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ix) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{1}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Root ke andar \(x^{2} + 4 = x^{2} + 2^{2}\) hai: 'square plus square', yani Case 2, \(x = 2\tan\theta\).
Bahar \(x^{2}\) bhi hai, jo \(4\tan^{2}\theta\) ban jayega.
Sab simplify karne par \(\frac{1}{4}\int\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin^{2}\theta}d\theta\) bachta hai, jo \(\sin\theta\) ki ek aasaan substitution hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: substitute, integrate, phir right triangle bana kar wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: Case 2, \(x = 2\tan\theta\). Wajah: \(1 + \tan^{2}\theta = \sec^{2}\theta\) root ko khatam kar deta hai.

\(x = 2\tan\theta\) rakhein, \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = 2\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{x^{2}+4} = \sqrt{4\tan^{2}\theta+4} = 2\sec\theta\]
Kyun: 4 common, phir identity; is interval mein \(\sec\theta\) positive hai.

Simple karein
\[I = \int\dfrac{2\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta}{(4\tan^{2}\theta)(2\sec\theta)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\int\dfrac{\sec\theta}{\tan^{2}\theta}\,d\theta\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\int\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin^{2}\theta}\,d\theta\]
Kyun: \(\frac{2}{8} = \frac{1}{4}\); ek \(\sec\theta\) cancel hua. Phir \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\) aur \(\tan^{2}\theta = \frac{\sin^{2}\theta}{\cos^{2}\theta}\) likha.

Integrate karein (\(v = \sin\theta\), \(dv = \cos\theta\,d\theta\))
\[\dfrac{1}{4}\int v^{-2}\,dv = -\dfrac{1}{4v} + c\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{4\sin\theta} + c\]
Kyun: numerator \(\cos\theta\,d\theta\) bilkul \(dv\) hai; power rule \(n = -2\).

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{x}{2} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\]
\[I = -\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}{4x} + c\]
Kyun: ek right triangle sochiye jis mein opposite side \(x\), adjacent side 2 ho; Pythagoras se hypotenuse \(\sqrt{x^{2}+4}\). Phir \(\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\).
Dhyan dein: jawab \(\theta\) mein chhor dena adhoora hai; hamesha wapas \(x\) mein likhein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big(-\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}{4x}\Big)\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2}+4}} - \sqrt{x^{2}+4}}{x^{2}}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{x^{2} - (x^{2}+4)}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+4}}\]
Kyun: quotient rule se asal integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (x) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{dx}{(1+x^{2})^{3/2}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Power \(\frac{3}{2}\) ka matlab hai \((\sqrt{1+x^{2}})^{3}\); andar 'square plus square' hai, \(a = 1\).
Is liye Case 2: \(x = \tan\theta\). Phir \(1 + x^{2} = \sec^{2}\theta\) aur \((1+x^{2})^{3/2} = \sec^{3}\theta\).
Integral sirf \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta\) reh jata hai.
Find karna hai indefinite integral.
Plan: substitute, integrate, triangle se wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{(1+x^{2})^{3/2}}\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: Case 2, \(x = \tan\theta\), kyunke \(1 + \tan^{2}\theta = \sec^{2}\theta\).

\(x = \tan\theta\) rakhein, \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = \sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\]
\[1 + x^{2} = \sec^{2}\theta\]
\[(1+x^{2})^{3/2} = \sec^{3}\theta\]
Kyun: \((\sec^{2}\theta)^{3/2} = \sec^{3}\theta\), kyunke yahan \(\sec\theta\) positive hai.

Integrate karein
\[\int\dfrac{\sec^{2}\theta}{\sec^{3}\theta}\,d\theta = \int\cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[= \sin\theta + c\]
Kyun: \(\sec^{2}\theta\) cancel hua aur ek \(\sec\theta\) neeche bacha; \(\frac{1}{\sec\theta} = \cos\theta\).

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[\tan\theta = x \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}} + c\]
Kyun: right triangle mein opposite \(x\), adjacent 1, hypotenuse \(\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\sin(\tan^{-1}x)\) likh kar chhor dena adhoora jawab hai; isay algebraic shakal mein badlein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{1+x^{2}} - \frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}}{1+x^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{(1+x^{2})^{3/2}}\]
Kyun: quotient rule se integrand mil gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (xi) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\)
blocks.explanation:
Root ke andar \(x^{2} - 9 = x^{2} - 3^{2}\): 'variable square minus constant square', yani Case 3.
\(x = 3\sec\theta\) rakhne se root \(3\tan\theta\) ban jata hai aur sab cancel ho kar \(\frac{1}{3}\int d\theta\) bachta hai.
Yeh part (vi) jaisa hi hai, bas wahan pehle 3 bahar nikalna para tha.
Find karna hai indefinite integral; \(x > 3\) lete hain.
Plan: substitute, integrate, wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\), \(x > 3\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: Case 3, \(x = 3\sec\theta\), kyunke \(\sec^{2}\theta - 1 = \tan^{2}\theta\) root ko khatam karta hai.

\(x = 3\sec\theta\) rakhein, \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = 3\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{x^{2}-9} = \sqrt{9\sec^{2}\theta - 9} = 3\tan\theta\]
Kyun: 9 common, identity, aur is interval mein \(\tan\theta\) positive.

Simple kar ke integrate karein
\[\int\dfrac{3\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta}{(3\sec\theta)(3\tan\theta)} = \dfrac{1}{3}\int d\theta\]
\[= \dfrac{\theta}{3} + c\]
Kyun: \(\sec\theta\tan\theta\) upar neeche cancel; \(\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}\).

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[\sec\theta = \dfrac{x}{3} \Rightarrow \theta = \sec^{-1}\dfrac{x}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + c\]
Kyun: yeh Challenge box ke formula (v) se bhi milta hai, \(a = 3\).

Answer key wali shakal
\[\tan\theta = \sqrt{\sec^{2}\theta - 1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{\theta}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}{3}\]
Kyun: is liye key ka \(\frac{1}{3}\arctan\left(\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}{3}\right) + c\) bhi \(x > 3\) ke liye yahi jawab hai. (\(x < -3\) ke liye \(\frac{1}{3}\sec^{-1}\left|\frac{x}{3}\right| + c\) likhein, jaise Example 28 mein.)
Dhyan dein: \(\sec^{-1}\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) wali dono shaklein sahi hain; ek ko ghalat na samjhein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\tfrac{1}{3}\sec^{-1}\tfrac{x}{3}\Big] = \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{3}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^{2}-9}}\]
Kyun: integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.prompt: 2 (xii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Poora fraction root ke andar hai; seedha koi formula nahi lagta.
Trick: root ke andar upar neeche \((1+x)\) se multiply karo. Upar perfect square \((1+x)^{2}\) ban jata hai aur neeche \(1 - x^{2}\).
Ab integrand \(\frac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\) hai, aur \(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\) Case 1 hai: \(x = \sin\theta\).
Find karna hai indefinite integral; \(-1 \le x < 1\) par yeh defined hai.
Plan: rationalise, \(x = \sin\theta\), \(\int(1+\sin\theta)d\theta\), wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}\,dx\), \(-1 \le x < 1\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: denominator ko \(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\) banayenge, phir Case 1, \(x = \sin\theta\).

Rationalise karein
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(1+x)^{2}}{(1-x)(1+x)}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\]
Kyun: \((1-x)(1+x) = 1 - x^{2}\). Aur \(1 + x \ge 0\) hai, is liye \(\sqrt{(1+x)^{2}} = 1 + x\) (minus ka khatra nahi).

\(x = \sin\theta\) rakhein, \(-\frac{\pi}{2} \le \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
\[dx = \cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \cos\theta\]
\[\int\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\cdot\cos\theta\,d\theta = \int(1+\sin\theta)\,d\theta\]
Kyun: \(1 - \sin^{2}\theta = \cos^{2}\theta\), aur is interval mein \(\cos\theta \ge 0\). \(\cos\theta\) cancel ho gaya.

Integrate karein
\[= \theta - \cos\theta + c\]
Kyun: \(\int 1\,d\theta = \theta\), \(\int\sin\theta\,d\theta = -\cos\theta\).
Dhyan dein: \(\sin\theta\) ka integral \(-\cos\theta\) hai, \(+\cos\theta\) nahi.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[\theta = \sin^{-1}x,\quad \cos\theta = \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\]
\[= \sin^{-1}x - \sqrt{1-x^{2}} + c\]
Kyun: \(x = \sin\theta\) se; \(\cos\theta = \sqrt{1-\sin^{2}\theta}\).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\sin^{-1}x - \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\Big]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}}\]
Kyun: integrand wapas mil gaya. (Bina trigonometry ke bhi ho sakta hai: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} + \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\) alag alag integrate karein.)

blocks.prompt: 2 (xiii) Evaluate the following integral (by change of variable): \(\int \frac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\,dx\ (a > 0)\)
blocks.explanation:
Root ke andar \(a^{2} - x^{2}\) hai: 'constant square minus variable square', yani Case 1, \(x = a\sin\theta\).
Root \(a\cos\theta\) ban jata hai, aur integral \(a\int\frac{\cos^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}d\theta\).
\(\cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \sin^{2}\theta\) likh kar do aasaan terms ban jate hain: \(\csc\theta\) aur \(\sin\theta\).
Find karna hai indefinite integral; \(a > 0\) diya hai.
Plan: substitute, split, integrate, triangle se wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\,dx\), \(a > 0\)
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: Case 1, \(x = a\sin\theta\), kyunke \(1 - \sin^{2}\theta = \cos^{2}\theta\) root ko khatam karta hai.

\(x = a\sin\theta\) rakhein, \(-\frac{\pi}{2} \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\theta \ne 0\)
\[dx = a\cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}} = a\cos\theta\]
Kyun: \(a^{2} - a^{2}\sin^{2}\theta = a^{2}\cos^{2}\theta\); is interval mein \(\cos\theta \ge 0\). \(\theta \ne 0\) is liye ke \(x\) neeche hai aur zero nahi ho sakta.

Simple karein
\[I = \int\dfrac{a\cos\theta}{a\sin\theta}\cdot a\cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[= a\int\dfrac{\cos^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}\,d\theta = a\int\dfrac{1-\sin^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}\,d\theta\]
\[= a\int(\csc\theta - \sin\theta)\,d\theta\]
Kyun: fraction ko do hisson mein toda: \(\frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \csc\theta\) aur \(\frac{\sin^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta} = \sin\theta\).

Integrate karein
\[= a\ln|\csc\theta - \cot\theta| + a\cos\theta + c\]
Kyun: \(\int\csc\theta\,d\theta = \ln|\csc\theta - \cot\theta|\) (yaad rakhne wala formula) aur \(-\int\sin\theta\,d\theta = +\cos\theta\).
Dhyan dein: \(-\sin\theta\) ka integral \(+\cos\theta\) hai; sign ulat jata hai.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[\csc\theta = \dfrac{a}{x},\quad \cot\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\]
\[a\cos\theta = \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\]
\[I = a\ln\left|\dfrac{a-\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\right| + \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}} + c\]
Kyun: \(\sin\theta = \frac{x}{a}\) se triangle: hypotenuse \(a\), opposite \(x\), adjacent \(\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\). \(\csc\theta - \cot\theta\) ko ek fraction mein likha.

Tasdeeq
\(a\ln|a - \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}| - a\ln|x| + \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\) ka derivative:
\[\dfrac{ax}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\,(a - \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}})}\]
\[- \dfrac{a}{x} - \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\]
Pehle fraction ko \(\frac{a+\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{a+\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\) se multiply karein to \(\frac{a(a+\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}})}{x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\) banta hai; teeno ko jor kar \(\frac{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}{x}\) milta hai. Sympy se bhi check kiya.
